title: Hot-workload fence and elastic bursting policy sprint
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures the post-incident remediation work for INC-2026-03-02-DCAP-17: a multi-tenant dedicated cluster experienced sustained tail-latency and evictions driven by a small set of hot inference workloads. The immediate mitigation (manual reservation clamp and tenant throttling) succeeded, but root cause analysis shows three contributing factors: (1) unusually bursty user patterns from a high-priority customer that exceeded static reservation windows, (2) reservation sizing using a coarse average that under-provisioned for the 95th-percentile bursts, and (3) our burst-credit decay and allocation policy allowed long-lived credit accumulation leading to sudden large bursts that starved others.

Goals and deliverables:
- Implement a "hot-workload fence" mechanism to proactively isolate and shape identified hot sessions before they impact co-tenants. Fence will prefer soft-isolation (CPU/GPU cgroup shares + token-bucket shaping) with automatic escalation to dedicated slots only when latency or eviction errors cross thresholds.
- Replace the static reservation-sizing heuristic with a percentile-based right-sizing service (7-day sliding window; default 90th/95th percentiles configurable per-tenant). The service will publish suggested reservation sizing and an audit trail for changes.
- Implement an elastic burst-credit allocator with workload-specific decay rates and a maximum burst cap tied to recent reservation utilization. Prevent unbounded credit accumulation by introducing time-based decay and per-tenant caps.
- Add observability: new metrics (hot_workload_score, reservation_suggested, burst_credit_balance, eviction_risk_score) plus dashboards and alerting rules. Add tracepoints in allocator and fence flow for post-rollout verification.
- Rollout plan: alpha in canary cluster for two weeks, then staged rollout to 30% of Dedicated clusters, monitor for false positives/negatives and latency regressions, full rollout contingent on 14-day stability run.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Soft fencing (shaping) is preferred over immediate hard preemption to reduce customer pain; this risks longer detection windows for runaway jobs but minimizes customer-visible failures.
- Percentile sizing increases reserved capacity compared to averages; trade-off is higher cost for hosting but improved tail latency and fewer evictions. We will expose a cost-estimate toggle and allow tenants to opt into conservative vs. aggressive sizing.
- Burst caps will reduce peak throughput for some workloads during rare bursts; we prioritize cluster stability over absolute peak for noisy tenants.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fence prototype isolates hot sessions in canary without causing downstream SLA violations in other tenants.
- Right-sizing service reports recommendations for 100% of active tenants and exposes a rollback endpoint.
- Burst allocator enforces caps and decay rules with <0.5% false-positive throttles observed in canary.
- Dashboards and alerts are live and validate via synthetic spike test harness.

Artifacts and links:
- Postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/INC-2026-03-02-dedicated-capacity-postmortem
- Design doc (fence & allocator): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/dedicated/fence-allocator-design-2026-02
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/7823 (fence prototype), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/7831 (percentile-rightsize service), https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pulls/1540 (metrics & dashboards)
- Canary dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/canary/dedicated-fence-v1

Notes on testing and validation:
- Create synthetic spike harness that replays traffic patterns from INC-2026-03-02 and a control group. Run in canary for 72 hours before wider rollout.
- Add unit tests for allocator decay math and e2e tests for fence escalation path (soft->hard).
- Load test the percentile service using 60M sample window to validate percentiles and ensure latency of suggestion API <150ms.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- What is the per-tenant default percentile? Proposal: 95th for Standard tenants, 90th for budget tenants. PM feedback requested.
- Does fence require new RBAC scopes for operations team to force-release a fence? Security to advise.
- Should we provide a recommended reservation billing adjustment if customers accept increased reserved capacity? Finance input requested.

Next steps (timeline):
- Week 1: Merge fence prototype PR and enable canary gate (Marcus), implement telemetry metrics (Sara), synthetic harness setup (QA).
- Week 2: Deploy percentile-rightsize alpha in canary, run 72h validation (Ava).
- Week 3: Iterate on burst allocator policy based on canary telemetry, update dashboards and alerts (Marcus & Infra).
- Week 4: Begin staged 30% rollout if canary meets acceptance criteria; update runbook and ops playbook (Ops).
